subject: Urgent: Atlas AI - intermittent streaming stalls suspected proxy throttling
messages:
From: Atlas AI Support <support@atlasai.com>
To: rohan_mehta@redwood.ai
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 14 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: live stream interruptions during demo window

Hi Rohan / Redwood team,

We're seeing frequent interruptions on streaming responses from your hosted API during our morning peak (14:00-15:30 PST yesterday). Symptoms:
- Long tail latencies (10–30s) followed by a final 502 or a silent connection drop.
- Effects most visible on chunked-transfer responses and websocket streams used in our live demo.
- Our load balancer logs show repeated RST_STREAM/stream-reset events and half-closed TCP flows; payloads tend to be ~1.1–1.5MB per session before the stall.

We've attached a small sample of request IDs and timing (atlas_incident_sample_requests.csv) and a short text trace. This is customer-facing — we had 18 demo failures in a 90-minute window yesterday which is impacting our rollout.

Ask: can you triage urgently and propose a remediation path? We need either a technical workaround we can apply on our side or a mitigation you can deploy while you investigate root cause. Renewal conversations are scheduled next week, so we need to demonstrate reliability this week.

Thanks,
Atlas AI Support
---
Atlas AI | support@atlasai.com
From: rohan_mehta@redwood.ai
To: Atlas AI Support <support@atlasai.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 14 Nov 2026 09:35:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: live stream interruptions during demo window

Thanks for the report and the samples — I’m sorry for the disruption. I’ve opened a high-priority incident on our side (INF-4821) and looped in CS and Live Ops. Immediate plan:
1) Monica/CS will contact your SRE to collect any extra request IDs and confirm whether you see any CDN/proxy translation in front of the client flows.
2) Marissa/Live Ops and I will pull server-side traces for the listed request IDs and check for chunk framing errors, chunk coalescing, and keepalive resets.
3) Short-term mitigation we can offer: we can route your traffic to a dedicated pool (isolated capacity) and enable a per-customer fallback that forces short-chunk flushes and tighter websocket heartbeats. This will require a short configuration change on our side and restart of the edge proxy for your tenant (expected < 10 minutes of impact if we perform it during a low minute window).

Can you confirm a 30-minute window today when we can apply the config change? Also, please confirm whether you have any customer-side HTTP proxies/CDNs that might be re-chunking responses.

I'll keep you posted as we get traces.

—Rohan Mehta
Director, Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference
rohan_mehta@redwood.ai
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>, rohan_mehta@redwood.ai
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 14 Nov 2026 13:07:00 -08:00
Subject: Internal: initial triage notes for Atlas AI (INF-4821)

David / Team — quick summary of what I see after a first-pass on the traces attached by Atlas:
- We are seeing repeated pattern where server emits chunked frames but the TCP connection receives an intermediate FIN from the client-proxy during the middle of the stream. That leaves the server write queue in a half-flushed state and the runtime's chunk-assembly logic stalls waiting for the final chunk terminator.
- Packet snippet (attached) shows an out-of-order FIN + ACK sequence from the customer-side proxy ~8–12s into the session in multiple samples.
- No immediate OOM/worker crash on our side; CPU/mem profiles look healthy. This appears to be an intermediary (proxy/CDN or an enterprise edge) aborting/reshaping the stream.

Proposed immediate mitigation (low-risk, short rollout):
- Canary a runtime patch that will: 1) detect an abrupt FIN during chunk assembly and emit a zero-length chunk + immediate FIN on our side to force client-side parsers to complete, 2) add a per-tenant circuit-breaker that will failover streaming requests to a short-polling mode (poll for tokens rather than relying purely on chunked websockets) for 5 minutes after N anomalies.
- Operational mitigation: move Atlas traffic to a dedicated pool (this avoids noisy neighbor queueing and gives us a fast rollback path).

I can do a canary deploy to 5% traffic in us-west-2 in the next 2 hours if we get approval. We’ll need an ETA window from Atlas for the config switch so we can coordinate. Attaching traces: trace-20261114.txt, packet-snippet.pcap.

Action items:
- David: please validate that the zero-length-chunk response behavior will be interpreted correctly by clients (particularly the customer's proxy variants). If you can smoke-test against a proxy emulator and confirm no new regressions, let me know and I’ll push the canary.
- Monica: confirm customer availability for the window and coordinate an exec-brief if they request one.

Marissa Cole
Sr. Product Operations (Live Ops) | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
From: Jane Liu <jane.liu@atlasai.com>
To: rohan_mehta@redwood.ai
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Mark Peterson <mark.peterson@atlasai.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 17:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: live stream interruptions during demo window

Rohan / Monica — thanks for the quick response. We appreciate the immediate triage steps, but given the customer-visible failures and the timing of our renewal, I’m elevating this to request an executive-level briefing.

Can we schedule a 30-minute briefing tomorrow morning PST with your engineering lead and someone from product/ops to go over:
- Root cause hypothesis and planned mitigations (what you’ll change and rollback plan)
- Short-term customer impact mitigation (what we can enable quickly)
- Timeline to prevent recurrence and targeted SLA uplift if we route to dedicated pool

We cannot afford more demo failures next week. Mark, feel free to propose times.

Best,
Jane Liu
VP, Partnerships | Atlas AI
